The NPA: Tell no lies, claim no easy victories

By: Chwayitisa Futshane | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The NPA says they are not in a crisis, but to date despite promises they have not won a single case. In a challenging interview we ask the leadership what they are doing wrong

Unique Selling Point:
Spicy interview with the head of the NPA Shamila Batohi, and her deputy, the former head of the Independent directorate and several other high profile interviews, internal meeting recordings of the NPA


Summary:
In 2019 Shamila Batohi returned from the Hague to lead the National Prosecuting Authority. During the Zuma presidency, the once proud NPA had been hollowed out by state capture.

Batohi was a welcome appointment. She promised to restore the NPA and ensure speedy convictions of the state capture perpetrators. That same year, Hermione Cronje was appointed to head up the Investigating Directorate, the sharp end of the NPA that would investigate, arrest and prosecute those responsible.

Batohi and Cronje -two powerful women, with the same aim- to hold those accountable for bringing the South African state almost to its knees. But within two years, Cronje left the NPA for a second time. Cronje is a straight shooter. She believed that there was a crisis in the NPA and that Batohi wasn’t leading effectively enough to turn it around. She believes the crisis in the NPA is ongoing. In an interview she says:

My personality is such that I don't have great finesse so if I see a problem I will call it out. And you're free to disagree with me. You can tell me that I have the wrong understanding of the problem, but I want the space to be able to say that this is the problem I'm experiencing, and I think we need to address it.

Cronje says there were powerful and corrupt people still inside the organisation attempting to sabotage her work, one of these was Knorx Mollele. The NPA eventually charged him but it came too late -by then, Cronje had already left. He should have faced criminal charges, but instead the leadership made a deal with him and eventually he left, only to reinvent himself as head of Lesotho’s anti-corruption unit. The bad apples in the NPA were just one of Cronje’ s concerns. Another was the serious lack of skills to prosecute complex corruption and money laundering crimes and the spin they were putting out instead, of doing the real hard yards. Now as Batohi tells the public that impunity is no longer a given, and the NPA is fit for purpose, those comments are undermined by the facts. The NPA has not to date won a single state capture case.

“There's far too much emphasis on we've got to look like we're winning this battle. It is important to look like we're winning the battle, but it has to be based on interventions that actually is going to ensure that we win the battle !”

Glynnis Breytenbach who supported Batohi’s appointment is scathing. “Just give us one win!” she told her recently, “and we will all go away.” But alas there are no high profile perpetrators in orange overalls. And as for the Gupta’s they are long gone, any cases they had to answer to, are currently dead, so if you see them at Heathrow, wave them by. There are no Interpol red notices out for their arrests, and no charges against the state capture mastermind.

Further information:
Susan
Do you think that you've been tough enough for this job?
Shamila: I don't think what I think about myself is important. I think I leave the people of this country and for you all to make your very considered judgments on that and let the work speak for itself.

Internal recordings of Shamila Batohi speaking to her staff in 2022 reveals a leader that was optimistic. She speaks of popping champagne within months. And in those heady days of 2022, a string of high profile arrests earned Cronje’s replacement, Andrea Johnson -a person of the year accolade. But arrests are not convictions, and as one state capture case after another has failed, or has been struck off the roll, even the cartoonists began to weigh in. Shamila Batohi has been depicted riding on a snail, or sleeping on the beach.

Susan
Speaking of priorities, though, I want to read you something else that you said in 2022. You said, “let's forget about the next six years. The next year is going to be the defining moment for the NPA the next six months. And I've said this publicly, my focus as the national director is going to be how do we deliver on Zondo? Our focus is Zondo Commission.” So to say now that it's 0.01% of your work feels quite convenient now that those cases are not going anywhere.
Shamila
Does it mean it's still not our focus? There's nothing different at all. It is our focus. It has remained. In fact, when I came back from The Hague in 2019, I knew dealing with state capture matters will sadly be the defining thing for the NPA. And I say sadly, right, because it's an important aspect, but people will forget about the really other, /the 99% of crime rebuilding that I talked about.

THE STATE CAPTURE CASES

Nulane, the first and easiest state capture case should have been a cinch, but the judge called it a comedy of errors and struck it from the roll. Matshela Koko, the former Eskom executive predicted the NPA would embarrass themselves and he was right. After six years of investigations, three postponements, and no charges after a year, the judge let him and his family go. The Transnet locomotive case – a R54 billion rand corrupt deal comes to court in January after three years. But Glynnis Breytenbach believes the NPA have the wrong strategy and she isn’t holding her breath. “And they keep on taking matters to court with ten and 11 and 12 accused -It's madness! You can't win a case like that! The first time they appear, one accused will have an ingrown toenail and it must get postponed! Second time someone's got a pimple on his nose, must get postponed! And when you work your way through the 12 accused, then the defence start being sick. So it just never comes to trial.

The latest case is that of former cabinet minister Zizi Kodwa. Arrested in June, but six months later the charges are withdrawn by the DPP of Gauteng who Batohi asked the president to suspend. Here is a sample of the tone of the entire interview with Batohi
Susan
Well, let's talk about the Zizi Kodwa case, that high profile arrest gets taken to court, six months later, the charges get withdrawn?
Shamila
So the national director had nothing to do with that decision. We are reviewing that decision because it is a high profile case.
Susan
Now, you a year ago asked the president to suspend advocate Chauke. Isn't it your job if the president doesn't act, to kick up the fuss, to say this is not okay?
Shamila
Do you know whether I'm kicking up a fuss or not?
Susan
I don't know, are you publicly calling out the president and saying…Shamila interrupts
Shamila
It's not my job to kick up a fuss! It's my job to do what a national director is required to do in this position responsibly and ethically. And that is what I'm doing.
Susan
The fact, though, that he took the decision to withdraw the charges, it potentially points to the fact that there are bad actors within the NPA who are failing, who are undermining the system from within, doesn't it?
Shamila
That's an assumption you're making. I must look at the facts of this case and then decide, which I will do.
Susan
The other option is that it didn't go through a review panel, and that the NPA once again brought a case to court that was half baked?
Shamila
So I must now look at the evidence without making any assumptions about it, and objectively decide whether the DPP's decision was correct or not.
Susan
Are you concerned that a year has passed since you asked the president to suspend advocate Chauke, and that a decision has still not been taken?
Shamila:
Of course I am! It is unfair on the institution. It is unfair on the individual concerned. We need this matter to be put to bed, whatever it is, if the president decides on an inquiry so be it. If he decides on no inquiry, so be it.

In a wide ranging interview that pulls no punches, Susan Comrie challenges Shamila Batohi on why the NPA has not delivered on state capture cases.

CARTE BLANCHE NPA SCRIPT FOR FINAL MIX
VO 1
In 2019 Advocate Shamila Batohi was appointed to lead the NPA.

State capture had decimated both the country and the prosecuting authority, so Batohi’s appointment was a welcome relief.

And she promised the nation to put those responsible, behind bars.

Shamila Up sound Press conference
We are acutely aware of what the people of South Africa want

VO 2
That same year former NPA prosecutor Hermione Cronje took the reins of the Investigating Directorate, the arm of the NPA that would investigate and prosecute state capture crimes

Hermione up sound
There are a lot of things that you see in a docket that you just can't fathom

VO 3
Two powerful women with the same aim. But their alliance wouldn't last. Within three years of working under Batohi, Cronje left the NPA for a second time.

Hermione
I am deeply frustrated, as are most South Africans who are desperate for real good news stories coming out of the NPA.

VO 4
Now Batohi’s former deputy can no longer remain silent.

Hermione Cronje
I don't think it's helpful to sugarcoat. We really are in a crisis!

VO 5
Susan and Sam walking in and or Susan on Ipad
I am Susan Comrie, an investigative journalist for AmaBhungane. This investigation is a look at recent high profile state capture cases and why the NPA is failing to successfully prosecute them.

FADE TO BLACK



VO 6
In December 2021, lack of skills, lack of strategy and internal sabotage prompted Cronje to leave the NPA

She was replaced by seasoned prosecutor Andrea Johnson
Who became a household name as a member of the prosecuting team in the Oscar Pistorius trial.

Johnson came in guns blazing. Suddenly there were multiple high profile arrests - Transnet, Eskom, a former cabinet minister.

In a meeting with staff in 2022, Batohi was in a celebratory mood.

Shamila_Champagne.mp4 (shorter)
Shamila: After six months, we're going to be celebrating and popping lots of champagne.

NULANE TITLE ON TEAR

VO 7
The first state capture case the NPA would take to court was Nulane. It was a R25 million rand feasibility study that would persuade the Free State government to release half a billion rand into an equally controversial scheme known as the Estina dairy project - the omens weren’t promising.

Hermione
The bottom line is we didn't have the capacity, we didn't have the skills in house.

Jan 2023 Bloemfontein High court title

VO 8
In January last year, the Nulane trial got underway, But the case soon began to unravel. Senior News24 journalist, Karyn Maughan was in court.

Karyn
There was such a profound lack of seriousness from some of those investigators that it was mortifying. The basics required of any successful prosecution simply weren't done.

VO 9
The judge called it a comedy of errors and hammered the NPA for how it had investigated the case

Hermione
That criticism is devastating. Admitting documents into evidence, that's trial work 101. Right? And the fact that the judge thought we were hopeless at that is devastating.

VO 10
When cases like this go wrong it's Batohi’s job to get them back on track

Susan
Why did you not intervene when you saw that the case was going off the rails?
Shamila:
How do you know I didn't?
Susan:
Well did you?
Shamila (sarcastic)
That would have been a good first question!
Susan
But did you intervene?
Shamila:
Of course I did. There are lots of things that happen behind the scenes, because we understand the reputational damage for an NPA when these cases fail
Susan: Why were those interventions not successful?
Shamila:
I have no idea right. I cannot say because we did the best we could.

VO 11
In April 2023, the Courts dismissed all charges against the accused.
Beat
The NPA is now left hoping for a retrial, and there is a good chance that may never happen.

VO 12
At the height of state capture, Matshela Koko was one of Eskom’s most powerful executives.

In October 2022, Koko, his wife and his stepdaughter were arrested for an allegedly corrupt multibillion rand tender connected to the Kusile power station.

But the arrests were premature because their investigation was incomplete.

Sam Sole leads Amabhungane centre for investigative journalism

Sam Sole
it's easy to arrest people, it's not that easy to bring them to trial and to have a successful prosecution. And that is what counts. You reduce confidence in the organisation if you arrest people and then you can't follow through.

VO 13
After a third postponement the magistrate struck the Koko case from the roll and told the NPA to come back when they were ready.

Glynnis Breytenbach is a former senior NPA prosecutor and now a member of parliament.

Glynnis:
There's just no other way to describe it. you screwed up in Nulane, and now you've got Koko et al still on the roll and it gets struck off. I mean, struck off. How?! How is the National Prosecuting Authority not ready with their cases!?

VO 14
They weren't ready because they didn't hire forensic analysts to sift through hard drives seized from Koko’s premises

Susan
Why were the seizures not done first before bringing the case to court?
Shamila
That is a very good question. We've learned a lot of lessons from this, and that is I agree with you. I've said to prosecutors, let's ensure that these searches and seizures are actually done earlier so that we don't have the same problem.

VO 15
Unless the NPA brings this R2.5 billion rand corruption case back to court, Koko and his co-accused are off the hook.

Nulane and Eskom - two vital state capture cases - both failed in court within months of each other.

Sam Sole
The, in summary is, the NPA can't deal with complexity. They can't deal with complex commercial crime cases, and they don't know how to sequence their battles, sequence their targets, and prioritise.

VO 16
The NPA boasts about their many successes. They’ve enrolled 547 corruption cases and convicted 700 government officials, they say. But they just can't get a state capture conviction in the bag.

Shamila
Colleagues,if we do not deliver in the next six months on state capture cases relating to our SOE’S. No matter what else we do, the country will see us as not having succeeded.

VO 17
But now, after two years of disappointments, Batohi is now backtracking, calling state capture cases only “0.01% of the NPA’s work”.

Susan
To say now that it is 0.01 % of your work, feels quite convenient now that those cases are not going anywhere?
Shamila
Doesn't mean it's not our focus. There is nothing different at all

LINK
In August the Investigating Directorate against corruption became a permanent part of the NPA. This is the unit they hope will emulate the Scorpions and once and for all put state capture actors behind bars

VO 18
Matthews Sesoko is the head of investigations at IDAC, the arm of the NPA that investigates state capture crimes

Susan
So, the Eskom Transnet SAP contracts, that one is still under investigation?
Matthews
Yes.
Susan
The Transnet Neotel contracts, that one I assume is still under investigation
Matthews:
It's still under investigation.
Susan:
The transnet cutting edge contracts, the locomotive contracts,
The relocation of the OEMs. SAA Mumbai Lufthansa. uh, Denel?
Matthews
Still under investigation.
Susan
I mean, objectively, isn't the NPA in a worse position than it was two years ago?
Matthews Well, it depends from which vintage point you are looking at it, from where we are making quite a progress in these matters, these are complex matters. And you're dealing with the kind of accused who have all the resources to fight

VO 19
The NPA boasts that it has a much longer list of cases where arrests have been made. But arrests are not convictions

Shamila Batohi
We have enrolled 37 cases in the ID. We have an ex speaker of Parliament in court. We have an ex-president that's being prosecuted. We have the secretary general of a ruling party.
Susan
Sure. But you're saying delivery is getting a case enrolled. Now, a number of those cases have been brought to court, have been struck off the roll. We've got the Nulane case, the first major state capture case.
Shamila
How many more?
Susan
We've got the Estina case, struck off the roll. We've got the Koko case. We've got the charges being withdrawn on the EOH case. The Transnet case has been in court for two and a half years. That still hasn't proceeded to trial.
Shamila
That’s the way these systems and processes work. Nulane is under appeal. Right. Koko will be re-enrolled. Okay. Estina will be re-enrolled. In my view these are not not failings yet, they are serious setbacks that we have properly interrogated and that we are learning from. But they're not failures!

VO 20
But what of the family at the centre of the state capture narrative? The people alleged to have had undue influence of government and access to its riches because of their closeness to a former president: the Gupta’s.

Link Susan
If there is one thing that would change the sentiment around the NPA it would be bringing the Gupta’s back to stand trial, but instead we keep letting them slip through our fingers

Glynnis
We knew who the Guptas were, we knew what they had done. We knew what the implications were. We knew that we wanted to prosecute them. And yet they hopped on a plane and buggered off.

VO 20
The Gupta’s escaped to Dubai, and ever since South Africa has been trying to get them extradited. Then in May 2024, one of the Gupta brothers, Ajay, was arrested in India on an unrelated matter. The NPA had a second chance to capture the state capture mastermind.

Sam Sole
And were we ready? Did we have an indictment that featured AJ Gupta? Did we immediately have a docket that we could send to the Indian authorities to say, hold this man for us. We want to extradite him and we have a treaty with India? No, we are still trying to tread water, getting spin.

VO 21
With both the Nulane and Estina cases struck from the roll, even if the Guptas are caught again, there is no case we can use to extradite them.

Susan:
Do you think that you've been tough enough for this job?
Shamila:
I don't think what I think about myself is important. I think I leave it to the people of this country, and for you all to make your very considered judgments on that, and let the work speak for itself at the end ocf the day.

VO
And right now it's speaking volumes.


THE END

PROMO ONE

VO
A former NPA executive speaks out

Hermione Cronje
I don't think it's helpful to sugarcoat. We really are in a crisis!
VO
But the NPA rejects the suggestion they are in a crisis

Susan
Can you really say that you've delivered?
Shamila
I can say we've delivered, but we haven't over delivered by any stretch of the imagination.

PROMO TWO 21 seconds
VO
Pressure has been mounting on the national director of public prosecutions, after their state capture cases have been struck from the roll.
Susan
Why did you not intervene when you saw that the case was going off the rails?
Shamila:
How do you know I didn't?
Susan:
Well did you?
Shamila (sarcastic)
That would have been a good first question!
Susan
But did you intervene?
Shamila:
Of course I did

PROMO THREE 22 seconds

Sam Sole
it's easy to arrest people, it's not that easy to bring them to trial and to have a successful prosecution. And that is what counts.

VO
Is the NPA making high profile arrests but unable to get convictions in state capture trials?

Glynnis:
You screwed up in Nulane, and now you've got Koko et al still on the roll and it gets struck off. I mean, struck off. How?! How is the National Prosecuting Authority not ready with their cases!?

FINAL MIX VO 1 In 2019 Advocate Shamila Batohi was appointed to lead the NPA. State capture had decimated both the country and the prosecuting authority, so Batohi’s appointment was a welcome relief. And she promised the nation to put those responsible, behind bars. Shamila Up sound Press conference We are acutely aware of what the people of South Africa want VO 2 That same year former NPA prosecutor Hermione Cronje took the reins of the Investigating Directorate, the arm of the NPA that would investigate and prosecute state capture crimes Hermione up sound There are a lot of things that you see in a docket that you just can't fathom VO 3 Two powerful women with the same aim. But their alliance wouldn't last. Within three years of working under Batohi, Cronje left the NPA for a second time. Hermione I am deeply frustrated, as are most South Africans who are desperate for real good news stories coming out of the NPA. VO 4 Now Batohi’s former deputy can no longer remain silent. Hermione Cronje I don't think it's helpful to sugarcoat. We really are in a crisis! VO 5 Susan and Sam walking in and or Susan on Ipad I am Susan Comrie, an investigative journalist for AmaBhungane. This investigation is a look at recent high profile state capture cases and why the NPA is failing to successfully prosecute them. FADE TO BLACK VO 6 In December 2021, lack of skills, lack of strategy and internal sabotage prompted Cronje to leave the NPA She was replaced by seasoned prosecutor Andrea Johnson Who became a household name as a member of the prosecuting team in the Oscar Pistorius trial. Johnson came in guns blazing. Suddenly there were multiple high profile arrests - Transnet, Eskom, a former cabinet minister. In a meeting with staff in 2022, Batohi was in a celebratory mood. Shamila_Champagne.mp4 (shorter) Shamila: After six months, we're going to be celebrating and popping lots of champagne. NULANE TITLE ON TEAR VO 7 The first state capture case the NPA would take to court was Nulane. It was a R25 million rand feasibility study that would persuade the Free State government to release half a billion rand into an equally controversial scheme known as the Estina dairy project - the omens weren’t promising. Hermione The bottom line is we didn't have the capacity, we didn't have the skills in house. Jan 2023 Bloemfontein High court title VO 8 In January last year, the Nulane trial got underway, But the case soon began to unravel. Senior News24 journalist, Karyn Maughan was in court. Karyn There was such a profound lack of seriousness from some of those investigators that it was mortifying. The basics required of any successful prosecution simply weren't done. VO 9 The judge called it a comedy of errors and hammered the NPA for how it had investigated the case Hermione That criticism is devastating. Admitting documents into evidence, that's trial work 101. Right? And the fact that the judge thought we were hopeless at that is devastating. VO 10 When cases like this go wrong it's Batohi’s job to get them back on track Susan Why did you not intervene when you saw that the case was going off the rails? Shamila: How do you know I didn't? Susan: Well did you? Shamila (sarcastic) That would have been a good first question! Susan But did you intervene? Shamila: Of course I did. There are lots of things that happen behind the scenes, because we understand the reputational damage for an NPA when these cases fail Susan: Why were those interventions not successful? Shamila: I have no idea right. I cannot say because we did the best we could. VO 11 In April 2023, the Courts dismissed all charges against the accused. Beat The NPA is now left hoping for a retrial, and there is a good chance that may never happen. VO 12 At the height of state capture, Matshela Koko was one of Eskom’s most powerful executives. In October 2022, Koko, his wife and his stepdaughter were arrested for an allegedly corrupt multibillion rand tender connected to the Kusile power station. But the arrests were premature because their investigation was incomplete. Sam Sole leads Amabhungane centre for investigative journalism Sam Sole it's easy to arrest people, it's not that easy to bring them to trial and to have a successful prosecution. And that is what counts. You reduce confidence in the organisation if you arrest people and then you can't follow through. VO 13 After a third postponement the magistrate struck the Koko case from the roll and told the NPA to come back when they were ready. Glynnis Breytenbach is a former senior NPA prosecutor and now a member of parliament. Glynnis: There's just no other way to describe it. you screwed up in Nulane, and now you've got Koko et al still on the roll and it gets struck off. I mean, struck off. How?! How is the National Prosecuting Authority not ready with their cases!? VO 14 They weren't ready because they didn't hire forensic analysts to sift through hard drives seized from Koko’s premises Susan Why were the seizures not done first before bringing the case to court? Shamila That is a very good question. We've learned a lot of lessons from this, and that is I agree with you. I've said to prosecutors, let's ensure that these searches and seizures are actually done earlier so that we don't have the same problem. VO 15 Unless the NPA brings this R2.5 billion rand corruption case back to court, Koko and his co-accused are off the hook. Nulane and Eskom - two vital state capture cases - both failed in court within months of each other. Sam Sole The, in summary is, the NPA can't deal with complexity. They can't deal with complex commercial crime cases, and they don't know how to sequence their battles, sequence their targets, and prioritise. VO 16 The NPA boasts about their many successes. They’ve enrolled 547 corruption cases and convicted 700 government officials, they say. But they just can't get a state capture conviction in the bag. Shamila Colleagues,if we do not deliver in the next six months on state capture cases relating to our SOE’S. No matter what else we do, the country will see us as not having succeeded. VO 17 But now, after two years of disappointments, Batohi is now backtracking, calling state capture cases only “0.01% of the NPA’s work”. Susan To say now that it is 0.01 % of your work, feels quite convenient now that those cases are not going anywhere? Shamila Doesn't mean it's not our focus. There is nothing different at all LINK In August the Investigating Directorate against corruption became a permanent part of the NPA. This is the unit they hope will emulate the Scorpions and once and for all put state capture actors behind bars VO 18 Matthews Sesoko is the head of investigations at IDAC, the arm of the NPA that investigates state capture crimes Susan So, the Eskom Transnet SAP contracts, that one is still under investigation? Matthews Yes. Susan The Transnet Neotel contracts, that one I assume is still under investigation Matthews: It's still under investigation. Susan: The transnet cutting edge contracts, the locomotive contracts, The relocation of the OEMs. SAA Mumbai Lufthansa. uh, Denel? Matthews Still under investigation. Susan I mean, objectively, isn't the NPA in a worse position than it was two years ago? Matthews Well, it depends from which vintage point you are looking at it, from where we are making quite a progress in these matters, these are complex matters. And you're dealing with the kind of accused who have all the resources to fight VO 19 The NPA boasts that it has a much longer list of cases where arrests have been made. But arrests are not convictions Shamila Batohi We have enrolled 37 cases in the ID. We have an ex speaker of Parliament in court. We have an ex-president that's being prosecuted. We have the secretary general of a ruling party. Susan Sure. But you're saying delivery is getting a case enrolled. Now, a number of those cases have been brought to court, have been struck off the roll. We've got the Nulane case, the first major state capture case. Shamila How many more? Susan We've got the Estina case, struck off the roll. We've got the Koko case. We've got the charges being withdrawn on the EOH case. The Transnet case has been in court for two and a half years. That still hasn't proceeded to trial. Shamila That’s the way these systems and processes work. Nulane is under appeal. Right. Koko will be re-enrolled. Okay. Estina will be re-enrolled. In my view these are not not failings yet, they are serious setbacks that we have properly interrogated and that we are learning from. But they're not failures! VO 20 But what of the family at the centre of the state capture narrative? The people alleged to have had undue influence of government and access to its riches because of their closeness to a former president: the Gupta’s. Link Susan If there is one thing that would change the sentiment around the NPA it would be bringing the Gupta’s back to stand trial, but instead we keep letting them slip through our fingers Glynnis We knew who the Guptas were, we knew what they had done. We knew what the implications were. We knew that we wanted to prosecute them. And yet they hopped on a plane and buggered off. VO 20 The Gupta’s escaped to Dubai, and ever since South Africa has been trying to get them extradited. Then in May 2024, one of the Gupta brothers, Ajay, was arrested in India on an unrelated matter. The NPA had a second chance to capture the state capture mastermind. Sam Sole And were we ready? Did we have an indictment that featured AJ Gupta? Did we immediately have a docket that we could send to the Indian authorities to say, hold this man for us. We want to extradite him and we have a treaty with India? No, we are still trying to tread water, getting spin. VO 21 With both the Nulane and Estina cases struck from the roll, even if the Guptas are caught again, there is no case we can use to extradite them. Susan: Do you think that you've been tough enough for this job? Shamila: I don't think what I think about myself is important. I think I leave it to the people of this country, and for you all to make your very considered judgments on that, and let the work speak for itself at the end ocf the day. VO And right now it's speaking volumes. THE END PROMO ONE VO A former NPA executive speaks out Hermione Cronje I don't think it's helpful to sugarcoat. We really are in a crisis! VO But the NPA rejects the suggestion they are in a crisis Susan Can you really say that you've delivered? Shamila I can say we've delivered, but we haven't over delivered by any stretch of the imagination. PROMO TWO 21 seconds VO Pressure has been mounting on the national director of public prosecutions, after their state capture cases have been struck from the roll. Susan Why did you not intervene when you saw that the case was going off the rails? Shamila: How do you know I didn't? Susan: Well did you? Shamila (sarcastic) That would have been a good first question! Susan But did you intervene? Shamila: Of course I did PROMO THREE 22 seconds Sam Sole it's easy to arrest people, it's not that easy to bring them to trial and to have a successful prosecution. And that is what counts. VO Is the NPA making high profile arrests but unable to get convictions in state capture trials? Glynnis: You screwed up in Nulane, and now you've got Koko et al still on the roll and it gets struck off. I mean, struck off. How?! How is the National Prosecuting Authority not ready with their cases!? VIDEO

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): The NPA says they are not in a crisis, but to date despite promises they have not won a single case. In a challenging interview we ask the leadership what they are doing wrong
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Spicy interview with the head of the NPA Shamila Batohi, and her deputy, the former head of the Independent directorate and several other high profile interviews, internal meeting recordings of the NPA
metadata.Summary: In 2019 Shamila Batohi returned from the Hague to lead the National Prosecuting Authority. During the Zuma presidency, the once proud NPA had been hollowed out by state capture. Batohi was a welcome appointment. She promised to restore the NPA and ensure speedy convictions of the state capture perpetrators. That same year, Hermione Cronje was appointed to head up the Investigating Directorate, the sharp end of the NPA that would investigate, arrest and prosecute those responsible. Batohi and Cronje -two powerful women, with the same aim- to hold those accountable for bringing the South African state almost to its knees. But within two years, Cronje left the NPA for a second time. Cronje is a straight shooter. She believed that there was a crisis in the NPA and that Batohi wasn’t leading effectively enough to turn it around. She believes the crisis in the NPA is ongoing. In an interview she says: My personality is such that I don't have great finesse so if I see a problem I will call it out. And you're free to disagree with me. You can tell me that I have the wrong understanding of the problem, but I want the space to be able to say that this is the problem I'm experiencing, and I think we need to address it. Cronje says there were powerful and corrupt people still inside the organisation attempting to sabotage her work, one of these was Knorx Mollele. The NPA eventually charged him but it came too late -by then, Cronje had already left. He should have faced criminal charges, but instead the leadership made a deal with him and eventually he left, only to reinvent himself as head of Lesotho’s anti-corruption unit. The bad apples in the NPA were just one of Cronje’ s concerns. Another was the serious lack of skills to prosecute complex corruption and money laundering crimes and the spin they were putting out instead, of doing the real hard yards. Now as Batohi tells the public that impunity is no longer a given, and the NPA is fit for purpose, those comments are undermined by the facts. The NPA has not to date won a single state capture case. “There's far too much emphasis on we've got to look like we're winning this battle. It is important to look like we're winning the battle, but it has to be based on interventions that actually is going to ensure that we win the battle !” Glynnis Breytenbach who supported Batohi’s appointment is scathing. “Just give us one win!” she told her recently, “and we will all go away.” But alas there are no high profile perpetrators in orange overalls. And as for the Gupta’s they are long gone, any cases they had to answer to, are currently dead, so if you see them at Heathrow, wave them by. There are no Interpol red notices out for their arrests, and no charges against the state capture mastermind.
metadata.Further information: Susan Do you think that you've been tough enough for this job? Shamila: I don't think what I think about myself is important. I think I leave the people of this country and for you all to make your very considered judgments on that and let the work speak for itself. Internal recordings of Shamila Batohi speaking to her staff in 2022 reveals a leader that was optimistic. She speaks of popping champagne within months. And in those heady days of 2022, a string of high profile arrests earned Cronje’s replacement, Andrea Johnson -a person of the year accolade. But arrests are not convictions, and as one state capture case after another has failed, or has been struck off the roll, even the cartoonists began to weigh in. Shamila Batohi has been depicted riding on a snail, or sleeping on the beach. Susan Speaking of priorities, though, I want to read you something else that you said in 2022. You said, “let's forget about the next six years. The next year is going to be the defining moment for the NPA the next six months. And I've said this publicly, my focus as the national director is going to be how do we deliver on Zondo? Our focus is Zondo Commission.” So to say now that it's 0.01% of your work feels quite convenient now that those cases are not going anywhere. Shamila Does it mean it's still not our focus? There's nothing different at all. It is our focus. It has remained. In fact, when I came back from The Hague in 2019, I knew dealing with state capture matters will sadly be the defining thing for the NPA. And I say sadly, right, because it's an important aspect, but people will forget about the really other, /the 99% of crime rebuilding that I talked about. THE STATE CAPTURE CASES Nulane, the first and easiest state capture case should have been a cinch, but the judge called it a comedy of errors and struck it from the roll. Matshela Koko, the former Eskom executive predicted the NPA would embarrass themselves and he was right. After six years of investigations, three postponements, and no charges after a year, the judge let him and his family go. The Transnet locomotive case – a R54 billion rand corrupt deal comes to court in January after three years. But Glynnis Breytenbach believes the NPA have the wrong strategy and she isn’t holding her breath. “And they keep on taking matters to court with ten and 11 and 12 accused -It's madness! You can't win a case like that! The first time they appear, one accused will have an ingrown toenail and it must get postponed! Second time someone's got a pimple on his nose, must get postponed! And when you work your way through the 12 accused, then the defence start being sick. So it just never comes to trial. The latest case is that of former cabinet minister Zizi Kodwa. Arrested in June, but six months later the charges are withdrawn by the DPP of Gauteng who Batohi asked the president to suspend. Here is a sample of the tone of the entire interview with Batohi Susan Well, let's talk about the Zizi Kodwa case, that high profile arrest gets taken to court, six months later, the charges get withdrawn? Shamila So the national director had nothing to do with that decision. We are reviewing that decision because it is a high profile case. Susan Now, you a year ago asked the president to suspend advocate Chauke. Isn't it your job if the president doesn't act, to kick up the fuss, to say this is not okay? Shamila Do you know whether I'm kicking up a fuss or not? Susan I don't know, are you publicly calling out the president and saying…Shamila interrupts Shamila It's not my job to kick up a fuss! It's my job to do what a national director is required to do in this position responsibly and ethically. And that is what I'm doing. Susan The fact, though, that he took the decision to withdraw the charges, it potentially points to the fact that there are bad actors within the NPA who are failing, who are undermining the system from within, doesn't it? Shamila That's an assumption you're making. I must look at the facts of this case and then decide, which I will do. Susan The other option is that it didn't go through a review panel, and that the NPA once again brought a case to court that was half baked? Shamila So I must now look at the evidence without making any assumptions about it, and objectively decide whether the DPP's decision was correct or not. Susan Are you concerned that a year has passed since you asked the president to suspend advocate Chauke, and that a decision has still not been taken? Shamila: Of course I am! It is unfair on the institution. It is unfair on the individual concerned. We need this matter to be put to bed, whatever it is, if the president decides on an inquiry so be it. If he decides on no inquiry, so be it. In a wide ranging interview that pulls no punches, Susan Comrie challenges Shamila Batohi on why the NPA has not delivered on state capture cases.
